newsitem.title: UK: UK directors not "fat cats" - IOD survey.
newsitem.headline: UK directors not "fat cats" - IOD survey.

text.p: The average British company director are not receiving larger percentage pay rises than their workers, the Institute of Directors (IOD) said on Thursday.

The company directors' organisation published a survey of salaries from data collected from its 5,000 members that showed basis pay rises in the board room rose an average of 3.7 percent and five percent in the past year, with a mid-range of four percent.
Just over one in 10 directors said their salary had been frozen.

"It confirms, once again that high-profile salaries and rises are not representative and give quite the wrong impression about directors' rewards generally," IOD director general Tim Melville-Ross said.

After taking bonuses into account and using a smaller sample, the report does show, however, that total earnings of chairmen rose 14 perent, managing directors 8.2 percent and other directors by 5.1 percent.
